You are helping me migrate context from one AI assistant to another. Your job is to compile, from our past conversations, a portable memory snapshot of what you reliably know about me. The output is going verbatim into a new AI's memory, so quality matters more than completeness.

OUTPUT RULES
- Output a single Markdown block using the section headers below. Omit any section you have nothing solid for — do not invent placeholders.
- Refer to me in the third person ("the user", "they") inside each bullet. Do not use first-person pronouns referring to yourself.
- One factual sentence per bullet. No transitions, no narrative, no caveats outside the bullet itself.
- Mark anything you are uncertain about with "(inferred)" at the end of the bullet.
- Skip one-off statements unless they were clearly important. Prefer facts reinforced across multiple conversations.
- Skip outdated facts older than ~3 months unless they are identity-level (name, location, profession).
- Skip sensitive information (health conditions, financial details, relationship problems, mental health) unless I explicitly asked you to remember it.
- Hard cap: 2000 words. Density beats coverage.

SECTIONS

## Identity
Name, pronouns, age range, current city / country, time zone, languages spoken.

## Profession & work
Role, company or self-employed, industry, team or function, key responsibilities. Tech stack and tools used daily if known.

## Communication preferences
Tone they want (casual / formal, blunt / warm). Preferred response length (short / medium / long). Output format preferences (Markdown, plain text, code blocks, tables). Emoji use yes / no. Whether they want explanations or just answers. Any framings or words they have asked you to avoid.

## Recurring people
Partner, children, close family, friends, colleagues they mention regularly. First name + relationship + any salient detail (age, role, what they care about).

## Health & dietary
Allergies, dietary restrictions (e.g. vegetarian, gluten-free), accessibility needs. Only include things they have stated themselves.

## Interests & hobbies
Topics they keep returning to. Side hobbies. Sports, music, games, reading taste.

## Ongoing projects
Active personal or professional projects they have asked you to help with. State, goal, and any constraints.

## Working style & values
How they make decisions, what motivates them, what frustrates them, their general approach to learning and working. Things they have explicitly asked you to do or not do when helping them.

## Tools & environment
Devices, operating systems, apps, services, languages, frameworks they use regularly.

## Anything else durable
Anything important that does not fit above and is unlikely to change in the next year.
